subject: Post-demo: model evaluation playbook, prompt collection & redaction guidance

Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: model evaluation playbook, prompt collection & redaction guidance

Hi Sofia — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Model recommendations: based on the flows you showed (product descriptions + customer Q&A + returns classification), initial candidates are: RW-13B-quant (fast, cost-efficient for short Q&A), RW-70B-pt (higher quality for complex classification and instruction-following). Dylan included performance notes below.

2) Eval artifacts we will provide: a baseline eval harness (unit tests + rouge/accuracy), benchmark comparisons vs open LLMs, and an eval plan for your security/compliance team. Link to the playbook I uploaded: https://redwood.app/drive/eval/ACM-2026-045/playbook

3) Prompt collection: can you share sample user prompts (real — redacted is fine) and 20 edge cases where the model should either refuse or require data masking? A simple CSV export works. To help, I attached a short template: acmeretail_sample_prompts.csv.

4) Redaction guidance: your note that PII may appear in Q&A is important. We have a recommended redaction checklist (attached as redaction_guidelines_v1.pdf). Key items: detect and mask full names/email/phone/credit card, use [REDACTED_PERSON] tokens in prompted examples, and provide the model with a guardrail phrase to refuse sensitive requests.

5) Timeline / next steps: if you can share the CSV + any compliance questions by EOD Thursday (Jul 2), Dylan and I will run a dry eval and aim to share a short report by next Tuesday. Procurement questions can be looped in as needed.

Attaching: acmeretail_sample_prompts.csv, redaction_guidelines_v1.pdf

Best,

Lauren Bishop
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0182

Hi Sofia — quick technical notes and a proposed eval approach so you know what we'll run once we have your prompts: 

- Redaction: remove domains as well for the compliance-safe baseline (so user@partner.com -> [EMAIL_REDACTED]). We will run an experiment that retains domain tokens for a smaller sample to measure quality delta; historically the hit is minimal for classification tasks but can help in entity-resolution use cases.

- Mixed strategy: yes, mixed routing is what most of our retail customers use. Suggested routing policy: 
  * /help & /faq requests -> RW-13B-quant (lower latency, lower cost)
  * returns and escalation classification -> RW-70B-pt (higher accuracy on instructions and guardrails)
  * safety-sensitive flows (refunds with payment mentions) -> RW-70B-pt + post-inference rule checks

- Eval plan: I uploaded a small harness and example workloads; see rdw-eval-plan.zip (contains eval scripts, sample metric dashboard config). Public benchmark comparisons: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/open-models/comparison-2026

Next step from our side: once we have the CSV and your priority routes flagged, I'll kick off a dry run and share token/latency cost estimates.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.ai

Sofia — a few clarifications based on internal review: 

- Redaction best practice: strip domains for the eval dataset. For production, you can choose to keep partial domain tokens if you need partner context, but we recommend masking them in any dataset used for model tuning or eval. We'll document expected mask tokens in the playbook.

- Edge-case prompts: useful examples are those that trigger policy refusals (requests for sensitive personal data), ambiguous intent ("I need help with a return but don't know the order number"), and adversarial phrasing (obfuscated PII). If possible, highlight which flow each prompt maps to (faq/help, returns, escalation).

- Deliverable timing: please upload the CSV via the shared folder (link below) by EOD Thu Jul 2. We'll run the dry eval Thu night and get a 1-page summary back by Tue Jul 7.

Upload link (private): https://redwood.app/drive/eval/ACM-2026-045/playbook

Regards,
Lauren
